answer: Forced Unique Provenance** requires each agent identity to derive its key from one verified hardware root. Registration records a random seed that the device signs; the registry grows as a vine of linked sessions, so a cloned key produces two divergent branches the next time either instance acts. Any vertex with conflicting histories is flagged and both copies freeze pending audit. Spoofing demands one physical device per identity, and a violet marker in the log permanently exposes the split to every peer.
